newsitem.title: UK: UK to legislate on work time after consulting - Lang.
newsitem.headline: UK to legislate on work time after consulting - Lang.

text.p: The government will only legislate to impose EU working hours rules on British industry after full consultation with the public, Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang said on Tuesday.
"We will of course obey the law until we secure a change. But we will only legislate after carrying out full public consultation on the issues and options," Lang said in a statement.
Earlier the European Court of Justice ruled that Britain must obey the rules, which include a maximum 48 hour average working week for many classes of employees.

Lang said that in legislating, the government would "aim to take advantage of the valuable derogations already secured and to preserve as much as possible of the flexibility that has been such an important element in the revival of the economy".
He said Britain would insist that the EU's Intergovernmental Conference addresses the issues raised by the court verdict.

"That means arguing both for measures to prevent any other "social engineering' directives being forced on the UK by similar manoeuvres, and requiring that the Working Time Directive in particular should no longer affect the United Kingdom," he said.
"The Prime Minister (John Major) has today written to EU (Commission) President Jacques Santer to press our case in the most unequivocal terms." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
